name: After § 14
title: REPORT on advancing towards a care society: addressing the gender care gap
part_text: 14a. Stresses that families constitute the primary and most immediate environment for the provision of care across generations; recalls that, as enshrined in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, parents have the primary responsibility for the upbringing and development of the child to ensure their healthy and safe growth, and that the best interests of the child must be a primary consideration in all decisions affecting them; calls on the Member States to recognise and support the essential contribution of intergenerational solidarity within families, including the role of grandparents in providing regular care and assistance to persons in need of care and support; underlines that such family-based care arrangements, deeply rooted in the cultural and social traditions of the Member States, contribute to social cohesion, demographic balance and the well-being of dependent persons; calls for appropriate recognition of these contributions within social and pension systems, while fully respecting the competences of the Member States and the principle of subsidiarity;
